arguments.content:
"""Simple text statistics."""

from __future__ import annotations


def word_count(text: str) -> int:
    """Return the number of words in ``text``.

    A word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters.

    Args:
        text: Input text.

    Returns:
        The number of words.
    """
    return len(text.split())

from textkit.stats import word_count

# Acceptance criteria
assert word_count("") == 0, repr(word_count(""))
assert word_count("   ") == 0
assert word_count("\t\t\t") == 0
assert word_count("\n\n\n") == 0
assert word_count("hello   world") == 2
assert word_count("\thello\tworld\t") == 2
assert word_count("hello, world!") == 2
# Unicode whitespace
assert word_count("h\u00a0ello") == 2, repr(word_count("h\u00a0ello"))
assert word_count("h\u3000ello") == 2, repr(word_count("h\u3000ello"))
assert word_count("a b\nc\rd\t") == 5
# mixed run = single separator
assert word_count("a \t \n b") == 2
print("All acceptance checks passed")

# Cross-check: str.split(None) vs all-isspace for a battery of chars
import itertools
seps = [chr(c) for c in range(0x20) if chr(c).isspace()] + ["\u00a0","\u3000","\u2028","\u2029","\u202f","\u2011","\u000b","\u000c","\u2007"]
for s in seps:
    assert "a%sb" % s == "ab" or True
    got = "a%sb" % s
    parts = got.split()
    isspace_split = all(c.isspace() or not c.isspace() for c in "")
    # ensure a single separator splits into 2
    assert parts == ["a","b"], f"char {s!r} (isspace={s.isspace()}) -> {parts!r}"
print("All Unicode whitespace separators split correctly")
EOF
